From d5059e52fd8bc624ec4255c9fa01a266513d126b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sean Wang <sean.wang@mediatek.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jan 2026 12:00:13 -0600
Subject: [PATCH] wifi: mt76: mt7921: fix potential deadlock in
 mt7921_roc_abort_sync

roc_abort_sync() can deadlock with roc_work(). roc_work() holds
dev->mt76.mutex, while cancel_work_sync() waits for roc_work()
to finish. If the caller already owns the same mutex, both
sides block and no progress is possible.

This deadlock can occur during station removal when
mt76_sta_state() -> mt76_sta_remove() -> mt7921_mac_sta_remove() ->
mt7921_roc_abort_sync() invokes cancel_work_sync() while
roc_work() is still running and holding dev->mt76.mutex.

This avoids the mutex deadlock and preserves exactly-once
work ownership.

Fixes: 352d966126e6 ("wifi: mt76: mt7921: fix a potential association failure upon resuming")
Co-developed-by: Quan Zhou <quan.zhou@mediatek.com>
Signed-off-by: Quan Zhou <quan.zhou@mediatek.com>
Signed-off-by: Sean Wang <sean.wang@mediatek.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260126180013.8167-1-sean.wang@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Felix Fietkau <nbd@nbd.name>

diff --git a/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7921/main.c b/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7921/main.c
index f42e40f9663d..42b9514e04e7 100644
--- a/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7921/main.c
+++ b/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7921/main.c
@@ -371,12 +371,15 @@ void mt7921_roc_abort_sync(struct mt792x_dev *dev)
 {
 	struct mt792x_phy *phy = &dev->phy;
 
+	if (!test_and_clear_bit(MT76_STATE_ROC, &phy->mt76->state))
+		return;
+
 	timer_delete_sync(&phy->roc_timer);
-	cancel_work_sync(&phy->roc_work);
-	if (test_and_clear_bit(MT76_STATE_ROC, &phy->mt76->state))
-		ieee80211_iterate_interfaces(mt76_hw(dev),
-					     IEEE80211_IFACE_ITER_RESUME_ALL,
-					     mt7921_roc_iter, (void *)phy);
+	cancel_work(&phy->roc_work);
+
+	ieee80211_iterate_interfaces(mt76_hw(dev),
+				     IEEE80211_IFACE_ITER_RESUME_ALL,
+				     mt7921_roc_iter, (void *)phy);
 }
 EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(mt7921_roc_abort_sync);
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of the Patch

The patch fixes a potential deadlock in `mt7921_roc_abort_sync()` by reordering operations and replacing a synchronous work cancellation with a non‑blocking one. The deadlock occurred because `roc_abort_sync()` held `dev->mt76.mutex` while calling `cancel_work_sync()` to wait for `roc_work()`, which in turn also held the same mutex – causing both sides to block indefinitely.

### Modifications in `drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/mt7921/main.c`

1. **Early return if ROC not active**  
   Added `if (!test_and_clear_bit(MT76_STATE_ROC, &phy->mt76->state)) return;` at the beginning. This avoids unnecessary work if no ROC session is in progress.

2. **Replaced `cancel_work_sync` with `cancel_work`**  
   Changed `cancel_work_sync(&phy->roc_work);` to `cancel_work(&phy->roc_work);`. This prevents waiting for `roc_work()` to finish, thus eliminating the mutex deadlock.

3. **Moved ROC cleanup outside the bit test**  
   Previously, the `ieee80211_iterate_interfaces()` call (which notifies interfaces that ROC is ending) was conditional on successfully clearing the `MT76_STATE_ROC` bit. Now that the bit is cleared early, the iteration is always performed after cancelling the timer and work, ensuring consistent cleanup.

### Relationship between the modifications

- The early bit check and return avoid executing the rest of the function when no ROC is running, reducing overhead and guarding against redundant operations.
- Replacing `cancel_work_sync` with `cancel_work` is the core fix for the deadlock. Since the work may still be running, the subsequent `ieee80211_iterate_interfaces()` remains safe because the `MT76_STATE_ROC` bit has already been cleared (so `roc_work` will skip its own ROC‑ending actions) and `cancel_work` ensures the work will not start a new ROC session.
- Together, these changes preserve the intended effect of `roc_abort_sync()` (forcefully aborting an ongoing ROC operation and notifying the mac80211 stack) while avoiding the mutex inversion that caused the deadlock.

Here is the commit message:
wifi: mt76: mt7921: fix potential deadlock in
 mt7921_roc_abort_sync

roc_abort_sync() can deadlock with roc_work(). roc_work() holds
dev->mt76.mutex, while cancel_work_sync() waits for roc_work()
to finish. If the caller already owns the same mutex, both
sides block and no progress is possible.

This deadlock can occur during station removal when
mt76_sta_state() -> mt76_sta_remove() -> mt7921_mac_sta_remove() ->
mt7921_roc_abort_sync() invokes cancel_work_sync() while
roc_work() is still running and holding dev->mt76.mutex.

This avoids the mutex deadlock and preserves exactly-once

Fixes: 352d966126e6 ("wifi: mt76: mt7921: fix a potential association failure upon resuming")
Co-developed-by: Quan Zhou <quan.zhou@mediatek.com>
Signed-off-by: Quan Zhou <quan.zhou@mediatek.com>
Signed-off-by: Sean Wang <sean.wang@mediatek.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260126180013.8167-1-sean.wang@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Felix Fietkau <nbd@nbd.name>

Here is the root cause:
The deadlock occurs because `mt7921_roc_abort_sync()` holds `dev->mt76.mutex` and then calls `cancel_work_sync(&phy->roc_work)` to wait for `roc_work()` to finish. However, `roc_work()` also acquires the same `dev->mt76.mutex`. If `roc_work()` is already running and holding the mutex, `cancel_work_sync()` blocks indefinitely waiting for the work to complete, while the work cannot proceed because it needs the mutex held by the caller. This creates a classic mutex deadlock between the caller and the workqueue.

Here is the patch:
 
 void mt7921_roc_abort_sync(struct mt792x_dev *dev)
 {
 	struct mt792x_phy *phy = &dev->phy;
 
+	if (!test_and_clear_bit(MT76_STATE_ROC, &phy->mt76->state))
+		return;
+
 	timer_delete_sync(&phy->roc_timer);
-	cancel_work_sync(&phy->roc_work);
-	if (test_and_clear_bit(MT76_STATE_ROC, &phy->mt76->state))
-		ieee80211_iterate_interfaces(mt76_hw(dev),
-					     IEEE80211_IFACE_ITER_RESUME_ALL,
-					     mt7921_roc_iter, (void *)phy);
+	cancel_work(&phy->roc_work);
+
+	ieee80211_iterate_interfaces(mt76_hw(dev),
+				     IEEE80211_IFACE_ITER_RESUME_ALL,
+				     mt7921_roc_iter, (void *)phy);
 }
 EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(mt7921_roc_abort_sync);
